analysisSummary: Reproduced in an isolated copy: DRIFT lines printed, exit 0, 'CLEAN — no drift.' The while-loop runs in a pipeline subshell; err()'s FAIL=1 is lost. Not framework-dependent.

Re-executed roleBody against the real agents/worker.md: body starts with the dispatch-note HTML comment. Regex ^<!-- only matches a comment preceding the # Role: line, which is the opposite of the real file layout. Tests only assert '# Role:' removal, so the gap is uncaught.

Verified by grep: four '<verbatim body>' occurrences in prompts/next.md, zero @role/dispatch-shapes references, while dispatch-shapes.md and execution-doctrine.md (both 'Normative — follow exactly') and registry.md mandate @role:. Functional either way, but two normative shapes for the same dispatch is exactly the drift the package bans.
Read the file directly: two consecutive '4.' steps. Trivial but real edit error introduced by this branch.
bun test reports 25 tests; changelog says 13. Verifiable factual error.

Mechanism is real (file-count vs task-count; archive only on SHIP), but the watchdog is explicitly 'reminder-grade' and normal flow (per-task files + SHIP archiving) makes the masking window narrow. Design-intent call for a human.

Both sub-claims verified in source, but each is a reminder-quality/approach tradeoff, and which dedupe semantics is intended (episode vs gap-count) is ambiguous between the header comment and the inline comment. Human should pick the intended contract.

Claim (hypothesis): execSync command injection via computeDocsDrift's cmd template. Disproved: both interpolations are a git-produced commit hash (output of `git log -1 --format=%H`) and the fixed default ref 'HEAD'; nothing user-controlled reaches the command string; role names in readFile are constrained to [a-z][a-z0-9-]* (no traversal).

Claim: tool_call in-place mutation + block-on-unresolved-return is unsafe. Disproved against pi extensions docs (lines 751-766): 'event.input is mutable. Mutate it in place to patch tool arguments before execution' and blocking via {block:true, reason} — exactly the extension's contract. Partial resolution before a block is inert (blocked call never executes; the model retries with fresh args).

Claim: before_agent_start return shape wrong. Disproved against docs (lines 521-549): returning {message:{customType, content, display}} injects a persistent message — matches. event?.cwd is not a documented field but the process.cwd() fallback yields the same project dir.

Claim: plan.md regexes mismatch the real format. Disproved live: on the actual .workflows/plan.md, done=4, total=4, context markers=4, computeHygieneDrift → {0,0}; header prose '(all tasks ✅)' does not match the status-line pattern. The done-regexp's optional colon vs total-regexp's required colon is asymmetric but unreachable in any format the prompts produce.
Claim: isDocsExempt over-exempts (e.g. docs/generator.ts). True in the literal sense but explicitly documented as a coarse reminder-grade filter; no correctness gate depends on it.

Claim: agentsDir via __dirname/../agents breaks when installed. Disproved: roles are package assets (registry/README describe agents/ as package content), package.json ships the directory; behavior is identical for repo and installed-package layouts.

Claim: single-mode vs tasks[] identity handling in resolveSubagentInput mis-rewrites when input.prompt equals a tasks[].prompt. Traced: each field gets its own loop iteration; after the first rewrite input.prompt !== f so the else-branch rewrites the task — both end up resolved. The duplicate-string case converges correctly.
